newsitem.title: SPAIN: FOCUS - Telefonica price raises sale worries.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Telefonica price raises sale worries.

text.p: The sale of the government's last 20.9 percent stake in Spain's Telefonica may be going well but the steep price of the shares already listed has so far discouraged institutional investors, analysts and traders said on Friday.

"The shares have had support in the run-up to the sale, and the retail segment has done well. But the institutions are not so convinced. (The shares) might prove difficult to place with those outside the lead-managers' immediate circle," a trader at a Spanish bank said.
So far interest in the 50 percent tranche of this last stake reserved for small investors looks as impressive as could have been expected for Spain's domestic telephone operator.
Just two days after orders started to be placed, retail demand had already covered the 85.54 million shares to be offered, unconfirmed press reports estimated.

"Telefonica's done really well, and the placement's going brilliantly. But it's going to be difficult convincing foreign investors to get in there," said a trader at a foreign brokerage who requested anonymity.
One Spanish analyst said that managers of the sale are rumoured to be trying to curb reports of the strong retail demand which is pushing up the price and adding to institutions' reluctance.

"The managers of the sale are not going to have problems getting rid of the shares among the banks and companies within those groups. But I've heard that those who are independent (of the placement) aren't too keen at these prices," she said.
Telefonica hit a fresh high on the first day of the offer, January 20, at 3,425 pesetas. The stock price had already climbed a spectacular 80 percent in 1996.
She agreed that reluctance was even more heightened among foreign institutions.
"It makes sense. The institutions don't even know what price they're going to pay until the last day, and they don't get all the bonus offers that the small investors do," she added.
Funds know both that the share price has been massaged in the run-up to the offer, and that the shares now fully reflect the company's value, a telecoms analyst said.
"On the basis of fundamentals, Telefonica is fully-valued at 3,300 pesetas. In that price you've got medium-term earnings growth, growth of foreign business, and all the other factors discounted."
Telefonica shares shifted down a gear on Friday but were still outperforming the share indices.
At 1445 GMT Telefonica was down 45 pesetas, or 1.33 percent, to 3,335, while the Ibex-35 index of leading shares was down 1.8 percent to 5,352.85.

The final retail price of the offer, to be decided on February 17, will be the lowest of three possibilities: the maximum price on February 10, a four percent discount on a February 17 reference price, or the institutional price, which will be set after Wall Street closes on February 17.
